newsitem.title: UK: Eurobond trade ideas - Spread tightening in yen.
newsitem.headline: Eurobond trade ideas - Spread tightening in yen.

text.p: Eurobond analysts' latest Eurobond trade ideas focused on dollars, lire and yen.
Yamaichi expected spreads to continue tightening in the Euroyen market after conditions started to improve last week.
This improvement has been concentrated in better credits, notably Export Import Bank of Japan, Japan Development Bank and the World Bank, and particularly at the longer end.

Sanwa International said the Canadian dollar curve will flatten considerably this year. The easing cycle looks like coming to an end and the wide cost of carry between two- and ten-year Canadian treasuries makes the long-end look appealing.
Following are latest trade ideas, compiled by Reuters:
EUROYEN
Yamaichi recommends:
BUY Japan Development Bank 2.875 pct 2006
SELL Japan Development Bank 6.50 pct 2001
STRATEGY This gives a pick-up in yield of around 114
b.p., compared with 105 b.p. towards the end of last year.
EUROLIRE
San Paolo recommends:
BUY Eurofima 10.40 pct 09/99
SELL European Investment Bank 7.45 pct 02/99
STRATEGY Over the past month EIB has outperformed
Eurofima by approximately 30 basis points in price terms.
EIB is expensive against the swap trading at around 25 b.p. through while Eurofima is cheap against both the swap and BTP, trading about seven b.p. and 15 b.p. through respectively).
This switch offers around a 20 b.p. pick up in yield. In addition, Eurofima (like EIB) trades on a bid/offer spread of around 25 b.p.
BUY European Investment Bank 9.60 pct 01/01
SELL European Investment Bank 7.55 pct 11/01
STRATEGY This switch continues to be attractive. Over
the past month the EIB 7.55 percent has outperformed EIB 9.60 percent by approximately 150 b.p. in price terms.

EIB 7.55 pct is expensive against the swap and the BTP, trading at around 43 b.p. and 22 b.p. through respectively. EIB 9.60 pct is cheap for a supranational trading at about 12 b.p. through the swap and around 15 b.p. through the BTP (offer side). It also represents about a 18 b.p. pick up in yield.
BUY BayernHypo 6.75 pct 02/02
STRATEGY This bond is cheap, offering a yield of about
6.65 pct. It is trading approximately flat to the swap and at around 37 b.p. over the BTP. It is also a new issue.
BUY Abbey National 8.375 pct 10/03
STRATEGY It is cheap against the swap and BTP (trading
respectively at around one b.p. over and 10 b.p. through). It also offers fairly good liquidity.
BUY Inter-American Development Bank 7.70 pct 02/04
STRATEGY In the past month this bond has underperformed
other issues in the same area by approximately 95 b.p. in price terms. This bond is cheap against the swap and the BTP (trading around nine b.p. and 15 b.p. thorugh).
EURODOLLAR
Paribas recommends:
BUY SNCF 6.50 pct 08/02
SELL UK 7.25 pct 12/02
OR IBRD 6.375 pct 05/01
STRATEGY At around 13 b.p. over the SNCF compares
favourably to the other issues with the UK at about +4 b.p. to the five-year and the IBRD at about -2 b.p. to the five-year.
EURO-AUSTRALIAN DOLLAR/EURO-CANADIAN DOLLAR SWITCH
Sanwa International recommends:
BUY EIB 7.25 pct 03/06 (C$)
SELL KfW 7.25 pct 02/07 (A$)
STRATEGY This switch offers a yield give-up of 84 b.p.

and is in line with their belief that the Canadian dollar curve will flatten this year. By contrast, they also recommend steepening trades in Australian government bonds as a cut in short-term interest rates is in prospect.

From an historical basis, the ten-year government bond spread came close to a strong resistance level of -55 b.p. (out of Australia into Canada) recently. The nearest it came was -64 b.p. and the spread is now starting to widen again.
--Johanna Vellender, London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7658
